summary: Benjamin Ide Wheeler was a linguist who studied at Colby–Sawyer College, Brown University, and Heidelberg University under Hermann Osthoff. His career included professorships at Cornell and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, before serving as president of UC Berkeley (1899–1919).

Benjamin Lewis Rice was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served as Principal of Central College of Bangalore (~1865–1868), held leadership roles in the Department of Public Instruction in Mysore (~1868–1883), and directed the Mysore Archaeological Department (~1884–1889).

Benjamin Rowland worked in art history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After earning his S.B. and Ph.D. at Harvard University, he served there as Associate Professor from 1930 to 1972 and curated Asian collections at the Fogg Art Museum.

Benjamin Schultze was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at the University of Halle in 1711. He later worked as a missionary for the Danish-Halle Mission (1719–1726) and served as a missionary and teacher with the SPCK in 1728.
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University and Yale University, and held a post at the University of Michigan around 2004.

Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thubten Champa.
Benjamín Preciado is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. His career includes posts at El Colegio de México, where he is attested in 1997 and served as director as attested in 2011.

Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo in 1915. He taught at Shukyo, Nihon, and Waseda Universities, served as president of Taisho University (1926), and headed the Sanko Research Institute.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Calcutta and Dhaka universities under Alfred Foucher and Haraprasad Shastri. He directed the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, and the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1927–1952).

Benoît Vermander works in Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen, and Centre Sèvres, he served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and became professor of religious sciences at Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Essers was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Amsterdam under Barend Faddegon and Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw, completing a Th.D. at the University of Groningen in 1952 under Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen.

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After receiving his Doctorat d'État from Paris, he taught Asian religions at Cornell, served as professor at Stanford (~1987–2006), and held a chair at Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He headed the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Japanese civilization at the Collège de France from 1979 to 1996.

Bernard Goldman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan and held an academic post at Wayne State University from around 1954 to 1986.
Bernard Pignède was a Tibetologist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Louis Dumont from around 1956 to 1958.

Bernard S. Cohn was an Indologist and historian/anthropologist. After degrees at Wisconsin and Cornell, he held posts at the University of Rochester (1960–1964) and the University of Chicago (1956–1960; Professor of Anthropology and South Asian History 1964–1995).

Bernard Williams was a philosopher educated at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He held major academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).

Bernd Barschel was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Halle under Karl Ammer and Johannes Mehlig, later working there as an assistant (1960–1970) before completing a Ph.D. and becoming a Lektor at Jena (1977).

Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian who held an academic post at the University of Oldenburg from around 1987 to 1994, and subsequently served on the faculty at Heidelberg University from approximately 2003 to 2020.

Bernfried Schlerath was an Indologist, Iranian specialist, and linguist. He studied at Frankfurt, Hamburg, and Mainz under Hermann Lommel, later serving as professor at the University of Marburg (1970) and Free University of Berlin (1974–1992).
